newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chemical firms reject union pay proposal.
newsitem.headline: German chemical firms reject union pay proposal.

text.p: German chemical employers on Wednesday rejected a proposal by the IG Chemie trade union aimed at breaking the deadlock on hotly-disputed sick payments within the 1997 wage talks.

Earlier, IG Chemie offered employers what it called a "compromise package" after negotiations broke down overnight on the issue of sick pay, which a law passed in October allows companies to cut from 100 percent of salary to 80 percent.

Under the proposal, sick pay would be maintained at 100 percent but firms would be able to claw back costs related to absenteeism by a reduction in the "thirteenth month" end of year bonus generally given to workers.

But Hans Paul Frey, business manager for the BAVC chemical employers federation, said during a break in talks that the reduction on offer -- cutting the bonus from a full month's salary to 95 percent -- was not enough.
Union and employer negotiators nonetheless continued talks on Wednesday afternoon on how the model proposed by IG Chemie could be modified to form the basis of an agreement.
The extent of the overall 1997 wage rise had not yet been discussed in talks that are expected to extend well into the evening.

Sources close to the talks had earlier said the chemical employers had been prepared to continue with full sick payments as long as individuals with high absenteeism rates were penalised in other areas, such as end of year bonuses.
IG Chemie, meanwhile, wanted any impact on bonuses to reflect the absenteeism of a company's whole workforce rather than just individuals.
The IG Chemie proposal put forward a system of absenteeism penalties that was based on a combination of individual and company sickness levels.
Negotiations for the 1997 wage claim, which would normally be held next spring, had been brought forward because of strong resistance by workers to the new sick-pay law.
Two earlier rounds of talks for the 590,000 workers in the industry have already collapsed on the issue of sick pay.

Sick pay is, however, only one issue on which agreement must be reached. IG Chemie has already rejected an offer by employers of a 2.5 percent wage rise as "completely unacceptable", demanding a 4.2 percent increase.
